title: On Attribution
standfirst: Why the house writes 'attributed to' rather than names.
body:
## The honest spectrum

Attribution is a spectrum, and the house writes where on that spectrum the evidence places an object — no further.

- **Attributed to** — the evidence points to a hand, but not conclusively.
- **Circle of** — made in the orbit of a master, perhaps by a pupil.
- **Manner of** — in the style of, but later.
- **Retains** — what survives on the object itself.

> An attribution is a claim about evidence, not a marketing statement.

When the maker is unknown, we say so. A hallmarked teapot is a documented maker's work; an unsigned astrolabe is an unsigned astrolabe. The record is the luxury.

title: Reading Patina
standfirst: How surfaces record time — and how to read the difference between age and damage.
body:
## Surfaces that testify

Patina is not dirt, and it is not damage. It is the chemical record of an object's environment over decades or centuries.

Bronze that has lived in air develops a stable, dark surface. Bronze that has been buried develops greens that cannot be hurried. Wood oxidises to a depth that polish cannot imitate. Leather darkens where hands rest.

The house examines every surface under raking light. We distinguish:

- **Age patina** — chemistry and time; to be preserved.
- **Wear** — the record of use; to be respected.
- **Damage** — event-driven loss; to be disclosed.
- **Restoration** — later intervention; to be documented and dated where possible.

> The surface is a document. Cleaning it can be an act of erasure.

title: Provenance, Honestly
standfirst: The chain of custody as a moral document.
body:
## The chain, and its gaps

A provenance is a chain of custody: maker to owner to owner to collector. Each link must be evidenced — an invoice, an inventory, a catalogue entry, a photograph.

Where a link is missing, the house writes **NOT DOCUMENTED**. We do not guess backwards from style or ambition.

- A full chain is rare and valuable.
- A partial chain honestly stated is worth more than a full chain invented.
- A gap is not a disqualification. It is a fact.

> The record is the luxury.

This is why the house presents provenance as an archival timeline, not a footnote.

title: Restoration vs Original
standfirst: When a repair is part of the history.
body:
## When a repair is history

A restoration is not a flaw to hide; it is an event in the object's life. The question is whether it was done well, and when.

The house records every known intervention with a date where possible:

- The desk's pre-1950 leg repairs are history, documented.
- The bowl's 2019 rim dent, raised by a conservator, is history, documented.
- Undisclosed restoration is deception, and the house will not offer objects with undisclosed interventions.

> Our rule: if we know it happened, you will read it here.

Original condition is rare and priced accordingly — but a well-documented repair does not shame an object. It testifies that someone cared enough to keep it working.
